findings.title: Account UI error message switched to single braces and ICU choice syntax, which i18next will not render
findings.body: The account console is a React app rendered through i18next, whose interpolation syntax is double braces. Other keys in this same file use it (e.g. `error-invalid-length-too-short='{{0}}' must have minimal length of {{1}}.`). This line changes `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}` to `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` and adds the Java MessageFormat plural `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`, which i18next does not understand. Users will see literal `{0}` and `{2,choice,...}` in the validation error. The double braces were not a verifier problem, since the verifier strips the `<!-- -->` the sanitizer inserts around them, so the change is unnecessary. Restore the `{{n}}` placeholders and use wording that does not depend on ICU choice.

findings.title: Admin UI error message switched to single braces and ICU choice syntax, which i18next will not render
findings.body: The admin console uses i18next, whose interpolation syntax is `{{name}}`. This line changes the existing `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}` placeholders to single braces and adds the Java MessageFormat `{2,choice,...}` plural, which i18next does not support. The admin UI will display literal `{0}` and `{2,choice,...}` to users for this validation message. The original double-brace form was already accepted by the verifier, so this change is a regression. Keep the `{{n}}` placeholders in this js-app file; the ICU plural only belongs in the Java-side theme message files.

findings.title: Lithuanian login translation replaced with an Italian sentence
findings.body: The new `loginTotpStep1` value, 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', is Italian. The file is the Lithuanian login bundle, so Lithuanian users will see Italian text on the OTP setup page. The previous Lithuanian text should be translated to match the new English wording, or the key left out so it falls back to English.

findings.title: Lithuanian account translation replaced with an Italian sentence
findings.body: `totpStep1` is set to 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian, in the Lithuanian account bundle. Lithuanian users will see Italian on the account console's OTP setup page. Provide a Lithuanian translation or omit the key so the English text is used.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese account message written in Traditional Chinese
findings.body: The new `totpStep1` value '在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：' uses Traditional characters (手機, 應用程式) and a full-width colon in the Simplified Chinese bundle. Simplified-Chinese users would expect 手机 and 应用程序. The text appears copied from the zh_TW login bundle, so it should be rewritten in Simplified characters.

findings.title: Stray 'n' typo left in the Danish HTML email body on a line this PR edits
findings.body:
The `identityProviderLinkBodyHtml` value contains `

nHvis du ikke vil forbinde disse konti...`. The leading 'n' is a leftover from a `\n` escape and will appear in the rendered email. This line is already being modified in this PR (the closing `

` is added), so the typo should be fixed in the same edit.

findings.title: Anchor check compares anchors by position, so reordered translations are falsely rejected
findings.body: santizeAnchors walks the translation's anchor tags and the English anchor tags in lockstep (`englishMatcher.find()` is called once per translation anchor). Translations often reorder clauses. For English `Click here or there` and German `Oder dort oder hier`, the first translation anchor (`href="y"`) is compared with the first English anchor (`href="x"`). That reports 'Didn't find anchor tag' for a valid translation and the loop breaks, so the remaining anchors are never checked. Matching should look up each translation anchor among the English anchors (e.g. as a multiset) instead of by position.

findings.title: Diff reporting can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when common prefix and suffix overlap
findings.body: The start/end scan for the error message is computed independently, so the common prefix and suffix can overlap. Example: value `aXa` sanitized to `a`. start becomes 1, end becomes 1, and `sanitized.substring(1, 1 - 1)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. The exception aborts verification of the whole file instead of reporting the illegal HTML. Clamp the end index so that start <= sanitized.length() - end, or compute the difference with a proper diff.

findings.title: Missing English counterpart or I/O failure is thrown as RuntimeException, bypassing the Mojo's error contract
findings.body: verify() is declared to throw MojoExecutionException and wraps I/O errors that way, but verifySafeHtml() throws RuntimeException on both the translation read (line 70) and the English read (line 79). A translation without a matching `_en` file, or any read failure, therefore escapes as an unhandled RuntimeException with a stack trace, aborting the whole verification run instead of producing a MojoExecutionException with the file name. Propagate these as MojoExecutionException, or record them as messages.

findings.title: No test checks that a valid translation produces no messages
findings.body:
All four new tests only assert that a specific violation is reported. Nothing verifies the accept path: a translation that uses allowed ``/`
` when English has HTML, a matching anchor, or a correct `{2,choice,...}` plural should yield zero messages. Without a negative fixture, false positives in the sanitizer (which the reordering and positional issues show are plausible) can regress without any test failing.

findings.title: Duplicate-key assertion weakened from exact match to hasItem
findings.body: The previous assertion `Matchers.contains(...)` required exactly the duplicate-key message. It was changed to `Matchers.hasItem(...)`, which also passes if extra unexpected messages are produced (for example from the new HTML checks running on the same fixture). If the extra checks should not fire for this fixture, the test should keep asserting the exact result; otherwise, the fixture should be made HTML-clean so the exact assertion still holds.
